title: Remote scheduled task creation command
description: Detects a Schtasks command requesting task creation with an explicit /s target. Process telemetry does not establish that the task was created successfully.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may create a scheduled task on another Windows system to execute code remotely or establish persistence.
hypothesis.rationale: Microsoft documents /s as the remote-system selector for schtasks /create and MITRE records scheduled-task creation for execution, persistence and privilege escalation; legitimate remote administration can use the same syntax.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify schtasks.exe commands that combine /create with a remote /s target while leaving local task creation, remote queries and unrelated processes unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Resolve the source administrator, remote target and task definition, then validate the action against an approved change.
steps: Baseline this signal with the responsible application or endpoint owner; legitimate use is expected, and this event alone is not a compromise verdict.
Confirm the command's result in follow-on process, file, registry or service telemetry; a process-start event records intent and does not prove successful execution.
Review the complete command line, source device, account, initiating process, remote computer and task name.
Inspect the task action, trigger, run-as identity and the target system's subsequent process activity.
Confirm a documented deployment or administration workflow; remove unauthorized tasks and contain affected systems when malicious.
false_positives: Approved remote administration, software deployment and maintenance workflows

validation.expected_outcome: Match remote schtasks create commands; do not match local task creation, remote query or deletion, other processes or incomplete commands.

limitations: This single-event signal does not establish malicious intent or successful execution. Renamed binaries, alternate tools, obfuscation and unlogged activity can evade the bounded predicates.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
